chapter_theme: The descent of power (சத்திநிபாதம்): when the soul is ripe, the Lord's grace-power, figured as an old woman, a hill-girl or the Goddess with flowing hair, comes to the blinded soul, removes its darkness, cuts its deeds, comes as the guru and makes it Siva. Worship of the Goddess with the Lord ends birth.
structure_note: The chapter opens with the riddle of the old woman and the blind old man (1514), explained in part by 1518, which repeats its third line with the Lord as subject. Grace as light in darkness runs through 1516, 1517, 1522 and 1529; the Goddess as girl and consort through 1519 to 1528; 1527 states the doctrine plainly.

1514.reading: The old woman who sat in the corner of the dark room, meaning to unite with the blind old man, removed his blindness, showed him many good qualities, charmed him and married him.
1514.nuance: A riddle verse. Tradition takes the old woman as the Lord's grace-power, hidden and ancient, the dark room as the soul's state under malam, and the blind old man as the soul blinded since beginningless time. Nothing in the verse names them; the chapter title and 1518 support the reading.

1515.reading: If one thinks on the direction of the sweet sense, it stands as nectar to those who know it as the true sense, and for those who know the clarity of the honeyed sense it becomes the field where the senses roam.
1515.nuance: புலன் (sense, or region) is played on in every line: தீம்புலன், ஆம்புலன், தேம்புலன், கோம்புலன். The words resist a firm reading; கோம்புலன் நாடிய கொல்லை is especially obscure. The plain thread is that grace becomes nectar to those who know.

1516.reading: Removing darkness and carrying one past countless births, the First grants grace so that grace never leaves; joined with the Lord of the celestials, one has a joy that never leaves the true thing.
1516.nuance: நீக்கி, நீங்கா repeats through the verse: grace removes and then does not leave. மருள்நீங்கா வானவர் கோன் is awkward ('the Lord of gods whose delusion is not removed' makes no sense of the Lord), and புலம்பயல் is obscure; the last two lines may be corrupt.

1517.reading: As a lamp brought into a room wrapped in darkness burns and shows the things there, so into the confusion of delusion come Nandi of the great flower, the Lord wrapped in grace, and the Mother.
1517.nuance: The dark room recalls 1514. The verse makes the coming of grace the coming of a pair, the Lord and the Mother (அம்மை), as the chapter's title, the descent of Shakti, would lead one to expect. மாமலர் நந்தி is read as Nandi (Siva) seated in the heart's lotus.

1518.reading: Charming and uniting, removing confusion, driving off and cutting away deeds, bringing forth joy, removing blindness and showing many good qualities, he granted the knowledge that shines with grace.
1518.nuance: Line 3 is 1514's line 3 word for word, but here the subject is masculine (புரிந்தானே), the Lord, where in 1514 it was the old woman. Together the two verses make the Lord and his power one agent. வெருட்டி (frightening, driving away) shows grace as also forceful.

1519.reading: The men who bathed at the Kanni ford have no thought of bathing in the Kanni ford; if they had the thought of bathing in the Kanni ford, there would be no other birth after.
1519.nuance: கன்னித் துறை is the sacred bathing place of the Virgin (Kanyakumari) and, by the verse's turn, an inner ford of the Goddess as Kanni. Those who bathe outwardly miss the bathing that ends birth. What the inner bathing is, yogic or devotional, the verse doesn't say.

1520.reading: He is red, dark, white and good green; those who fully understand will reach the Lord: love him, saying 'this is the one whose hand wears the hide of the huge elephant dark as kohl.'
1520.nuance: The four colours may be the colours of Siva's faces, of the elements, or of the Lord with Shakti (green is often hers); the verse gives no key. மைவென்று may be 'outdoing kohl in blackness'. The elephant-hide is the familiar emblem of Siva who flayed the elephant demon.

1521.reading: However many ages pass, they say the woman and he are the sole Lord; for those who worship him every day it becomes something shown, like a deed done in the hand.
1521.nuance: தையலும் தானும் தனிநாயகம் makes the pair one sovereign. கையிற் கருமஞ்செய் காட்டது is obscure: perhaps 'as plain as a thing done in one's hand', the sense taken here.

1522.reading: We have seen it: the light that followed both, the supreme light of the Supreme who rests from of old, the Lord with long matted locks where bees revel among flowers, stood removing darkness for those who stood and saw.
1522.nuance: இரண்டும் (both) may be the Lord and Shakti, or the two eyes, or sun and moon; பண்டுபண்டோயும் is unclear. The verse speaks as a witness (கண்டுகொண்டோம்), and the darkness removed is for those who stood and looked.

1523.reading: The sweet girl in her father's garden makes one know seven times seven births, and when all that stands within is gone, she becomes the ripe fruit that has beheld the First.
1523.nuance: The girl in her father's garden is taken as the Goddess, daughter of the mountain king, or as grace growing in the Lord's own field. அண்ணிக்கும் (who is sweet, or who draws near) and எண்ணிக்கும் are uncertain forms. கனி (fruit) suggests the ripeness that 1527 calls the balance of deeds.

1524.reading: For those who stand worshipping her with due honour, the hill-girl with rounded breasts, the tender creeper, cuts birth, grants great austerity, cuts forgetfulness and sets them to worship.
1524.nuance: குறப்பெண் (girl of the hill tribes) is a name for the Goddess as mountain-born, though it also recalls Valli. Worship of her leads back into worship (வழிபட வைக்கும்): grace both rewards devotion and produces it.

1525.reading: Hold fast to the Lord of the eight directions with her of flower-fragrant garland and curling hair; for those of knowledge who join there, it becomes possible to follow the steady blue light.
1525.nuance: தூங்கொளி நீலம் (the hanging or steady blue light) is traditionally the Goddess, often described as blue, or a light seen in meditation. ஆங்கது சேரும் (who join there) leaves the place unnamed.

1526.reading: If one draws near she gives a shoot of knowledge; even in bowing I bow strewing many flowers; the One whom nothing that approaches can know becomes the life of every world that approaches.
1526.nuance: The subject of line 1 is unstated, and அணுகிய தொன்றறியாத ஒருவன் may be the Lord who is unknown to what approaches, or the one who knows nothing of what has come near. The verse plays on அணுகு (approach).

1527.reading: When the two deeds stand evenly balanced, the sweet grace-power comes as the guru and removes many qualities; when one's own doing ends through the knowledge it gives, the three impurities end and one becomes Siva.
1527.nuance: The chapter's doctrine stated plainly: இருவினை ஒப்பு (balance of good and bad deeds) is the sign of ripeness for the descent of power, the power comes in the form of the guru, and தன்செயல் அற்றால் (when one's own agency ends) the three malas go. குணம்பல நீக்கி is read as removing the soul's bound qualities. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Kumaraguruparar's Kandar Kalivenba.

1528.reading: Thinking of her with flowing hair who makes fragrance in the place where there is neither night nor day, join her without a sound, and the Supreme, with no other care, will rule you.
1528.nuance: இரவும் பகலும் இலாத இடம் (the place of no night or day) is traditionally a yogic state beyond the moon and sun breaths, or the state beyond waking and sleep. குரவம் may be the kuravam flower or a sound; அரவஞ்செய்யாமல் (without noise) may mean silently, or without the serpent (kundalini) stirring. பராபரை is the supreme Goddess.

1529.reading: The evening lamp, the moon and the sun, and the lone flame, the Lord who lights the hall: the Lord who lit up knowledge entered me, lit up my flesh and stayed with me.
1529.nuance: விளக்கு (lamp, to light) runs through every line, from outer lights to the light that lights the body. ஊனை விளக்கி (lit up the flesh) makes the body itself the place grace shines, not something to be left behind. Sengalvaraya notes Appar's verse beginning மாசில் வீணையும் மாலை மதியமும், which also opens with the evening moon.

links.note: 1518 repeats 1514's line, 'removing blindness and showing many good qualities', but with the Lord as the doer where 1514 had the old woman, and adds that he cut away deeds and gave knowledge. It unlocks part of the riddle: the woman's act is the Lord's.

Both use the lamp entering a dark room. The Naladiyar makes it austerity before which sin cannot stand, and warns the dark returns when the oil runs out; Tirumular makes it the Lord and the Mother entering delusion, with no warning that the light fails.

Both treat good and bad deeds alike as what must be overcome, not good deeds as a ladder. The Kural says the two dark deeds do not cling to those who praise the Lord truly; Tirumular says grace descends when the two stand in balance.

1516 says the First removes darkness, carries one past countless births and joins one to the வானவர் கோன்; 1552 says the வானவர் கோன் keeps the penitent from suffering and grants that there is no birth (பிறப்பில்லை). In 1552 the title plainly names the Lord who ends birth, which supports reading the awkward வானவர் கோன் of 1516 the same way rather than as Indra.

1517 compares the coming of the Lord and the Mother into delusion to a lamp brought into a dark room; 1793 says Nandi, far off to those who would touch him, ends the darkness like the light of a lamp (விளக்கொளி) when the heart lies gathered in longing. The pair shows the lamp-in-darkness figure used for grace both as a descent from outside (புக்கெரிந்தாற் போல்) and as what the longing heart receives.

509 says there are many holy waters within the heart, and those who do not plunge into them wander over hollow and height; 1519 says those who bathed at the Kanni ford never thought of bathing in the Kanni ford, and if they did there would be no further birth. 1519 applies 509's inner tirtha to one named shrine, turning the famous outer bathing place into its inner counterpart.

Both name bathing at Kumari: 1519 (கன்னித் துறைபடிந் தாடிய) says the outer bathers lack the inner bathing that ends birth, and the Thiruppugazh song asks not to bathe at Kumari (குமரி கலித்துறை முழுகி) with a sorrowing mind and be mocked. In both the famous ford stands for an outward remedy the poet sets aside; Tirumular offers an inner ford, Arunagirinathar Murugan's feet.

1520 calls the Lord red, dark, white and green without giving a key; 1735 assigns colours to Sadasiva's five faces: crystal, saffron, collyrium (அஞ்சனம்), red and milk. Read together, 1735 supports taking 1520's colours as the colours of the Lord's faces, though the two lists do not match exactly (green is not among 1735's).

Both use the phrase சிறப்பொடு பூசனை: Kural 18 says festival and worship will cease, even for the gods, if the sky dries up; 1524 says the hill-girl, for those who stand doing worship with honour, cuts birth and sets them to worship (வழிபட வைக்கும்). Each makes worship depend on a giver outside the worshipper, rain in the Kural, grace in the Tirumanthiram.

725 says the speaker once held the body shameful, then saw the Highest had made it his temple and now cherishes it; 1529 says the Lord who lit up knowledge entered him, lit up his flesh (ஊனை விளக்கி) and stayed with him. 1529 carries 725's discovery further: the body is not only the Lord's dwelling but is itself made luminous by his entry.

source_issues: 1516 lines 3 and 4 (மருள்நீங்கா வானவர் கோன், புலம்பயல்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
